transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee; Priya Raman; Marcus Chen (Redwood) — Oliver Grant; Sofia Morales; DeShawn Price (Catalyst Freight)

Auto-Summary: Quick recap, runbook rehearsal, assign detailed regressions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we'll run through the latest scorecard first then the rollback rehearsal. priya's got the eval notes.
[00:18] Priya Raman: yeah hi, hi. so quick heads up — last night's batch of 3k prompts showed a bump in false positives on the "delivery change" intent, about 6.8% up from baseline 2.1. i think it's mostly prompt drift from the new domain examples.
[00:36] Oliver Grant: sorry can i jump in — 6.8 percent is across all locales? we saw it high in the midwest subset and also in spanish variants.
[00:48] Priya Raman: good question. yeah it's concentrated in midwest english and southern spanish dialects, we suspect the paraphrase augmentation introduced ambiguity.
[00:59] Sofia Morales: and to be clear, those false positives are when the model suggests diversion to a new hub? that's the UX we can't surface.
[01:12] Priya Raman: correct, it's recommending reroute without confirmation which fails our safety rule.
[01:18] DeShawn Price: can you share the exact examples? the infra team wants to see if it's latency/K V cache related or purely prompt semantics, cause sometimes kv-cache misses change generation.
[01:33] Priya Raman: yeah i'll paste a sample in the notes, but prelim looks semantic. though we did note tokenization differences when we swapped quantization profile for the canary model.
[01:45] Marcus Chen: just to orient — this is why we added the guardrail at the scoring layer: if reroute_confidence < 0.78 we block and escalate. looks like the new prompts pushed some legitimate cases below.
[02:01] Jordan Lee: okay, let's talk mitigation. priya, what's a quick patch vs longer-term?
[02:08] Priya Raman: quick patch: tighten the parsing extractor and add a second-stage rerank that uses a stricter entailment threshold. longer term: prune ambiguous augmentations from the prompt set and re-run the 5k regression with dialect splits.
[02:23] Oliver Grant: workflow question — if we push the quick patch, will we need a model rollout? can we do it at the routing/score layer so no heavy infra changes?
[02:33] Priya Raman: yes that's the plan — routing and reranker only so we avoid full model redeploy. it's a config change in the scoring pipeline.
[02:41] DeShawn Price: excellent, since we're trying to avoid another full dedicated node spin-up. we still want to validate perf impact though.
[02:49] Jordan Lee: on perf, priya had that baseline run for us?
[02:53] Priya Raman: yep. baseline 95th pct latency was 210ms on hosted with caching enabled. when we flip the more aggressive reranker we saw +30ms typical, and worst-case +90ms under burst.
[03:06] Sofia Morales: that might be okay for internal flow but mobile customers will notice. any way to keep it under 250ms 95th?
[03:14] Priya Raman: with batching tweaks and keeping the reranker narrow, yes — we can stay near 240ms 95th. also cache priming for common prefixes helps.
[03:24] Oliver Grant: what's the expected unit cost impact? we need to model cost vs latency tradeoff for our execs.
[03:29] Jordan Lee: i'll send a delta estimate for hosted vs a small dedicated pool (3 nodes) — should show break-even in heavy throughput after 6 weeks.
[03:37] Marcus Chen: i'll attach the cost sheet and a sensitivity tab.
[03:40] [04:00] Jordan Lee: next up — rollback/canary rehearsal. deShawn, do you want to lead the infra checklist?
[04:06] DeShawn Price: sure. first step is VPC peering validation. our test stub showed intermittent no-route errors last week. we need to re-run that with the new peering rules and confirm port 443 egress is open to the Redwood control plane.
[04:22] Jordan Lee: priya, on the model side, how do we do canary?
[04:26] Priya Raman: we do a 5% canary on the routing table for 48 hours, with alerting on key signals: false positive rate, latency delta, and user recoverability score. if any breach, auto-fallback to previous model variant. we also have a manual quick rollback button in the console.
[04:41] Sofia Morales: can you demo the console rollback next week?
[04:44] Jordan Lee: yeah we can schedule a short demo — 15 min.
[04:48] Oliver Grant: also want a dry-run where we simulate a rollback under load. not just the button but the sequence: circuit-break, drain sessions, promote fallback variant.
[04:59] Priya Raman: agreed. we'll run a rehearsal in staging and capture timing metrics; that will show drain time and cache rebuild cost.
[05:08] Marcus Chen: watch for cache warm-up amps — KV cache warming can add token cost and latency spikes. put a low-traffic window for the dry run.
[05:18] DeShawn Price: noted. i'll coordinate the on-call rota and set a 2-hour window.
[05:24] Jordan Lee: onboarding / security notes — catalyst asked earlier about KMS integration and audit logs. marcus?
[05:30] Marcus Chen: SOC2 docs are in the shared folder, i'll add the KMS integration note and specifics on customer-managed keys. also will include the retention policy for audit logs and token-level traces.
[05:41] Oliver Grant: perfect — can we get the SLA addendum for the pilot? we need a written target for 99.5 uptime and a rollback response SLA.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: i'll draft a pilot SLA addendum and ping legal.
[05:54] [06:00] Priya Raman: back to quality — prompt pruning plan: we propose removing 120 ambiguous augmentations, tighten the training paraphrase generator, and add heuristics for geographic idioms. we will then run the 5k regression with a per-locale breakdown.
[06:15] Sofia Morales: how long will that take? we need results before 2026-11-30 demo to ops.
[06:21] Priya Raman: with current infra we can finish within 5 business days. i'll prioritize the midwest and spanish splits.
[06:28] Oliver Grant: ok please include labeling of severity so we can triage.
[06:32] Priya Raman: will do. i'll also add confidence histograms to the CSV.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: any other blockers?
[06:41] DeShawn Price: one more infra item — we need to test connection draining with long-lived sessions; otherwise rollback can cause duplicated deliveries.
[06:50] Marcus Chen: add a metric for duplicate actions per 1k requests for the dry run.
[06:56] [07:00] Jordan Lee: chorus check — ok, let's recap and assign owners. priya does the regression run, oliver uploads edge cases, deShawn validates VPC and drains. marcus adds SOC2/KMS note and cost sensitivity. i'll send pricing and schedule rollback dry-run.
[07:20] Sofia Morales: thanks all. can you also capture the sample examples that caused the FP spikes? that helps product decisions.
[07:28] Priya Raman: yes will paste into the ticket and include suggested prompt edits.
[07:34] Oliver Grant: last quick Q — competitors: anthro- uh anthropic's approach will do a different rerank; are we confident on explainability for audits?
[07:46] Jordan Lee: yes, we have traceable scoring and we can produce per-decision confidence logs for audit.
[07:52] DeShawn Price: cool, make sure the log retention aligns with our compliance window.
[07:57] Jordan Lee: noted. final note — we uploaded a short runbook and a link to the security deck in chat: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/catalyst-freight/runbook and security: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-kms-note (see notes).
[08:12] Marcus Chen: ok i'll follow up with the SLA addendum and the cost sheet.
[08:17] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll reconvene next week same time.

End of transcript.
